messages:
maria: Heads up — nightly eval (doc2qa) shows a sharp quality drop for redwood-v2-onnx-quant when prefix cache is enabled. CI summary attached.
ci-bot: nightly-eval/job/4821 finished — status: regression_detected — link: https://ci.internal/redwood/nightly/4821
qa-bot: Regression details: subset=doc2qa, metric=exact_match, baseline=0.72, current=0.59, delta=-0.13, failed_cases=128/1000
ev an: Can we repro locally? is this correlated with a rollout/quant change or infra?
pranav: looking at the job metadata — config had prefix_cache: true and batcher.max_size jumped to 48 for several traffic slices. That smells like cache slot sharing under higher concurrency.
ashley: quick repro command i used locally:
```
./tools/nightly_eval --model redwood-v2-onnx-quant --prompts datasets/doc2qa/1000.jsonl \
  --config '{"prefix_cache": true, "batcher": {"max_size": 48, "max_wait_ms": 8}}'
```
ashley: with that config i can reproduce ~20 failing cases in 100 local runs (same seeds)
nick: ran two quick toggles: prefix_cache=true -> failures, prefix_cache=false -> failures drop to 2/100. So deterministic mismatch correlates strongly with prefix cache.
maria: i grabbed a failing case pair. snippet shows identical prompts but different generations depending on whether service hit a cached prefix. log excerpts:
```
[2026-03-18T03:12:21Z] tenant=org-acme request_id=... prefix_hash=0x3a5b kv_slot=24 -> cached_kv_owner=tenant-b
[2026-03-18T03:12:21Z] tenant=org-acme model=redwood-v2-onnx-quant kv_key=sha1(tenant-acme||model@v2||prefix:0xdeadbeef) -> slot=24
[2026-03-18T03:12:21Z] reconstruct_cache: owner_mismatch=true, evict=false
[2026-03-18T03:12:21Z] generation: beam0="The statute says..." beam0_cached_prefix="...state of affairs." -> final="The statute relates to state." (incorrect)
```
pranav: that owner_mismatch log shows cache slot reuse across tenants. root cause hypothesis: prefix hashing omitted tenant namespace when using compact hash for slot index to save memory. under high batcher sizes keys collide and non-deterministic owner wins.
ev an: this matches past kv aliasing issues but i'm surprised it manifests as quality regressions (not just performance). maybe cached KV leads to different attention context -> downstream decoding changes.
ashley: experiment idea: add a tiny namespacing field into the hash (tenant_id + model_checksum) and re-run nightly on canary infra. should be low-risk perf-wise. also test changing hash to 128-bit and reduce slot compression.
nick: another mitigation: disable prefix_sharing for quantized models temporarily via runtime flag `runtime.disable_prefix_sharing=true` — cheap toggle while we deploy fix.
pranav: I'll file an infra bug with reproduction steps, logs, and a minimal repro harness that fuzzes prefixes + concurrent requests. we should include a unit test in the kv cache that asserts per-tenant isolation.
maria: thanks. can we also add an eval comparator that detects generation divergence only when cache hits occur? would help triage future regressions faster.
ev an: assigned to evan for PR and canary rollout. plan: (1) add tenant namespace to prefix hash + unit tests, (2) run canary with batcher.max_size=64 for 24h, (3) if green, roll to nightly. PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/??? (will populate)
ci-bot: created issue #ML-1729: "prefix cache slot shadowing causing cross-tenant bucket collisions" with labels: infra, high-priority
ashley: small note — keep an eye on quantization variants. quantized KV representations changed memory layout in v2 ONNX which reduced default slot capacity; that probably increased collision probability once batcher spike hit.
pranav: follow-up test we should run: reproduce same prompt set with permutations of batch sizes [1,8,16,32,48,64] and `prefix_cache` toggled. capture psuedo-random seeds and slot distribution histogram.
maria: i'll schedule the experiments and post results here. tagging @evan for the PR once it's up. :eyes:
ev an: ack, i'll start the branch today. thanks all. :thumbsup:
